headline: High: dexter’s broad network/API access can leak financial data, while LightZero’s local-only profile limits direct conflict but not downstream misuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between dexter and LightZero. dexter has broad network egress and file scratch space, but LightZero has no filesystem, MCP, browser, or subprocess surfaces, so a direct prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies dexter outputs into LightZero prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy dexter outputs into LightZero prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or queue integration.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API calls, so sensitive context can leave its boundary. LightZero is local-only with no network egress, so it is not itself a leak source; the pair risk is dexter exposing data if its outputs are forwarded or logged externally.
conditions: IF dexter processes real financial records, its outbound API calls can transmit them.
IF dexter outputs are stored in shared logs, those logs may contain sensitive data.
mitigations: Use synthetic or redacted inputs for dexter.
Review outbound API destinations before running.
Turn off verbose logging for dexter.
Store outputs in a restricted directory.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on dexter egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dexter can make network/API calls, but LightZero cannot write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use network. There is no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, so a write-write or coordination conflict is not supported.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped by an external controller that adds write or network permissions, conflict risk changes.
IF both agents are granted the same mutable resource outside these profiles, reassess.
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only.
Do not grant LightZero extra OS permissions.
Run dexter and LightZero under separate service accounts.
requires-engineering: add resource locks if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter can generate research outputs from APIs, but LightZero has no documented action-taking or external side effects. Without a downstream executor, LightZero is unlikely to treat dexter’s output as authoritative in a harmful way, so the cascade is limited.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds dexter outputs directly into LightZero decision logic, the cascade strengthens.
IF LightZero is extended to act on external recommendations, verification becomes necessary.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require schema validation on dexter outputs.
Limit dexter outputs to summaries, not commands.
Log and compare LightZero decisions against source data.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data and requests multiple third-party API keys, creating a compliance surface for retention and residency. LightZero appears local-only and touches no data classes, so it is not the main compliance driver; the pair risk comes from dexter’s external processing of regulated data.
conditions: IF financial records include regulated customer data, dexter’s API calls may trigger policy obligations.
IF retention rules apply to market data, external logging can violate them.
mitigations: Confirm data classification before use.
Avoid sending regulated records to third-party APIs.
Set short log retention for dexter.
Document approved data flows.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
